title: Nyatiti (eight-string lyre)
summary: The nyatiti is the eight-string lyre of the Luo people of Kenya. A long wooden trough is covered with hide and pinned at the edges, short carved arms rise from it, and the strings are tied to a beaded crossbar. The player sits and plucks with both hands while a ring of small iron bells on the toe keeps the beat.
howToPlay: Eight strings run from the beaded crossbar to the bridge, the lowest on the left. Each lane marks a place to pluck a string.
Beads slide down the strings. Pluck the lane as the bead lands.
The round lane at the foot of the lyre is the toe rattle: tap it on the beat, as the player taps the bells with the foot.
Learn the rattle pattern first, then add the strings over it.
rules: The strings are tuned to an even seven-note scale, with the eighth string an octave above the first.
The patterns are played through twice.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Patterns count eight pulses, split into 3 + 3 + 2.
heritageNote: The nyatiti is the main instrument of Luo song in western Kenya, played to accompany praise and story. The player keeps a steady rattle with the toe while the hands answer one another on the strings.
